name: Chapter 3: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
description: Triads to Mendeleev, modern periodic law, IUPAC names above 100, s p d f blocks, and trends in radius, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, electronegativity

cards.term: Number of elements known in 1800 and in 1865?
cards.definition: 31 in 1800; 63 by 1865

cards.term: Why classify elements?
cards.definition: To study them systematically, rationalise known facts and predict new ones

cards.term: Update: NCERT says "at present 114 elements are known". Current count?
cards.definition: 118 elements, all officially named by IUPAC (NCERT itself says "up to 118" later)

cards.term: Dobereiner’s law of triads (1829)?
cards.definition: In groups of three similar elements, the middle element’s atomic weight ≈ average of the other two

cards.term: Name Dobereiner’s three triads.
cards.definition: Li, Na, K; Ca, Sr, Ba; Cl, Br, I

cards.term: Why was the law of triads dismissed?
cards.definition: Worked only for a few elements: seen as coincidence

cards.term: Who made a cylindrical table of elements, and when?
cards.definition: A.E.B. de Chancourtois (French geologist), 1862

cards.term: Newlands’ law of octaves (1865)?
cards.definition: In order of atomic weight, every eighth element resembles the first, like musical octaves

cards.term: Limitation of the law of octaves?
cards.definition: Held only up to calcium

cards.term: Award later given to Newlands?
cards.definition: Davy Medal, 1887, Royal Society

cards.term: Who independently proposed the periodic law in 1869?
cards.definition: Dmitri Mendeleev (Russian) and Lothar Meyer (German)

cards.term: What did Lothar Meyer plot?
cards.definition: Atomic volume, m.p. and b.p. vs atomic weight: a periodic pattern

cards.term: Mendeleev’s periodic law?
cards.definition: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights

cards.term: What did Mendeleev rely on most while classifying?
cards.definition: Similarities in empirical formulas and properties of compounds (oxides, hydrides)

cards.term: Why was iodine placed after tellurium though lighter?
cards.definition: To group it with F, Cl, Br by properties; Mendeleev suspected wrong atomic weights

cards.term: What were eka-aluminium and eka-silicon?
cards.definition: Gaps left by Mendeleev: later gallium and germanium

cards.term: Mendeleev’s predictions vs found
cards.definition: Eka-Al atomic weight (pred. 68): Ga: 70; Eka-Al density (pred. 5.9): Ga: 5.94 g/cm³; Eka-Al m.p. (pred. low): Ga: 302.93 K; Eka-Si atomic weight (pred. 72): Ge: 72.6; Eka-Si oxide / chloride: GeO₂ / GeCl₄

cards.term: Mendeleev’s table (Fig. 3.1): what did it look like?
cards.definition: Groups I–VIII in columns with oxide formulas (R₂O … RO₄); series in rows

cards.term: Why is Mendeleev credited over Meyer?
cards.definition: He published first, used broader properties, left gaps and made bold successful predictions

cards.term: Moseley’s observation (1913)?
cards.definition: A plot of \( \sqrt{\nu} \) (X-ray frequency) vs atomic number is a straight line; not vs atomic mass

cards.term: Modern periodic law?
cards.definition: Properties are periodic functions of atomic numbers

cards.term: Mendeleev vs modern periodic law: basic difference?
cards.definition: Atomic weight vs atomic number

cards.term: What is the periodic law really a consequence of?
cards.definition: Periodic variation in electronic configurations

cards.term: Naturally occurring elements, and which are found in pitchblende?
cards.definition: 94; Np and Pu (like Ac and Pa) occur in pitchblende

cards.term: Long-form table: number of periods and groups?
cards.definition: 7 periods, 18 groups (IUPAC, replacing IA … VIIA, VIII, IB … VIIB, 0)

cards.term: What does the period number tell you?
cards.definition: The highest principal quantum number (n) of the elements

cards.term: Why are lanthanoids and actinoids placed at the bottom?
cards.definition: To keep the table’s structure and keep similar elements in one column

cards.term: Whose work placed actinoids below lanthanoids? Element named after him?
cards.definition: Glenn T. Seaborg (Nobel 1951); element 106 Seaborgium (Sg)

cards.term: Why did IUPAC introduce systematic names?
cards.definition: Disputes over discovery credit, e.g. element 104: Rutherfordium (US) vs Kurchatovium (USSR)

cards.text: IUPAC roots: 0 = {{c1::nil}}, 1 = {{c2::un}}, 2 = {{c3::bi}}, 3 = tri, 4 = {{c4::quad}}, 5 = pent, 6 = hex, 7 = sept, 8 = oct, 9 = {{c5::enn}}.
cards.extra: Add "ium" at the end; symbol = first letters of the roots.

cards.term: Full table of roots (Table 3.4)?
cards.definition: nil, un, bi, tri, quad, pent, hex, sept, oct, enn

cards.term: IUPAC name and symbol for Z = 120? (Problem 3.1)
cards.definition: Unbinilium, Ubn

cards.term: IUPAC systematic name of Z = 104, 109, 114?
cards.definition: Unnilquadium (Unq), Unnilennium (Une), Ununquadium (Uuq)

cards.term: Official names of Z = 113 to 118?
cards.definition: Nihonium (Nh), Flerovium (Fl), Moscovium (Mc), Livermorium (Lv), Tennessine (Ts), Oganesson (Og)

cards.term: Elements named after Lawrence Berkeley Lab and Seaborg’s group? (Ex 3.7)
cards.definition: Lawrencium (103) and Seaborgium (106)

cards.term: Trap: how many letters in a temporary IUPAC symbol?
cards.definition: Three (e.g. Uuo); official symbols have one or two

cards.term: Number of elements in a period equals?
cards.definition: Twice the number of orbitals in the level being filled

cards.term: Where does the 3d series start and end?
cards.definition: Scandium (Z = 21), 3d¹4s², to zinc (Z = 30), 3d¹⁰4s²

cards.term: Why 18 elements in the 5th period? (Problem 3.2)
cards.definition: 5s, 4d, 5p = 1 + 5 + 3 = 9 orbitals → 18 electrons

cards.term: Why 32 elements in the 6th period? (Ex 3.4)
cards.definition: 6s, 4f, 5d, 6p = 1 + 7 + 5 + 3 = 16 orbitals → 32

cards.text: Lanthanoids: 4f filling from {{c1::cerium (Z = 58)}} to {{c2::lutetium (Z = 71)}}. Actinoids: 5f filling after {{c3::actinium (Z = 89)}}.

cards.term: Group 1 valence configuration?
cards.definition: ns¹ (Li [He]2s¹ … Fr [Rn]7s¹)

cards.term: Period and group of Z = 114? (Ex 3.5)
cards.definition: Period 7, group 14 (Flerovium)

cards.term: Element in period 3, group 17? (Ex 3.6)
cards.definition: Chlorine, Z = 17

cards.term: Basis of dividing elements into s, p, d, f blocks?
cards.definition: The orbital being filled by the last electron

cards.term: Two exceptions to block placement?
cards.definition: Helium (s-block but put with noble gases, 1s² closed shell) and hydrogen (placed separately)

cards.term: Why is hydrogen placed separately?
cards.definition: It can lose an electron like group 1 or gain one like group 17

cards.term: s-block: groups and configuration?
cards.definition: Groups 1 and 2; ns¹ and ns²

cards.term: s-block properties?
cards.definition: Reactive metals, low ionisation enthalpy, form 1+/2+ ions; never free in nature

cards.term: Which s-block compounds are not predominantly ionic?
cards.definition: Li and Be compounds

cards.term: p-block: groups and configuration?
cards.definition: Groups 13–18; ns²np¹ to ns²np⁶

cards.term: Representative (main group) elements are?
cards.definition: s-block + p-block

cards.term: Chalcogens and halogens are groups?
cards.definition: Chalcogens: 16; halogens: 17

cards.term: d-block: groups and general configuration?
cards.definition: Groups 3–12; (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻²

cards.term: d-block element with ns⁰?
cards.definition: Pd: 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰

cards.term: Typical properties of transition elements?
cards.definition: Coloured ions, variable oxidation states, paramagnetism, catalysts

cards.term: Which d-block metals lack most transition properties, and why?
cards.definition: Zn, Cd, Hg: (n−1)d¹⁰ns² (full d)

cards.term: Why "transition" elements?
cards.definition: They form a bridge between reactive s-block metals and less active groups 13, 14

cards.term: f-block general configuration?
cards.definition: (n−2)f¹⁻¹⁴ (n−1)d⁰⁻¹ ns²

cards.term: Lanthanoid and actinoid ranges?
cards.definition: Lanthanoids Ce (58) – Lu (71); actinoids Th (90) – Lr (103)

cards.term: Why is actinoid chemistry harder?
cards.definition: Many oxidation states; all radioactive; many made only in nanograms

cards.term: What are transuranium elements?
cards.definition: Elements after uranium (Z > 92)

cards.term: Group and configuration of Z = 117 and Z = 120? (Problem 3.3)
cards.definition: 117: group 17, [Rn]5f¹⁴6d¹⁰7s²7p⁵. 120: group 2, [Og]8s².

cards.term: Update: NCERT Problem 3.3 says Z = 117 is "not yet discovered". Status?
cards.definition: Discovered in 2010, named Tennessine (Ts) in 2016; Z = 120 is still undiscovered

cards.term: What fraction of elements are metals?
cards.definition: More than 78%

cards.term: Metals with very low melting points?
cards.definition: Mercury (liquid); gallium (303 K) and caesium (302 K)

cards.term: Non-metals with high melting points (exceptions)?
cards.definition: Boron and carbon

cards.term: Name the metalloids given in NCERT.
cards.definition: Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te

cards.term: Trend in metallic character?
cards.definition: Increases down a group; decreases left to right

cards.term: Increasing metallic character: Si, Be, Mg, Na, P? (Problem 3.4)
cards.definition: P < Si < Be < Mg < Na

cards.term: Group with a metal, a non-metal, a liquid and a gas at room T? (Ex 3.27)
cards.definition: Group 17 (At metallic, I solid non-metal, Br liquid, F/Cl gases)

cards.term: Why can’t atomic size be measured precisely?
cards.definition: Atoms are tiny (~1.2 Å) and the electron cloud has no sharp boundary

cards.term: Covalent radius, e.g. chlorine?
cards.definition: Half the single-bond distance: Cl₂ 198 pm → 99 pm

cards.term: Metallic radius, e.g. copper?
cards.definition: Half the distance between metal cores: 256 pm → 128 pm

cards.term: Why is atomic radius of noble gases not compared with others?
cards.definition: They are monatomic: their (van der Waals) radii are much larger than covalent radii

cards.term: Atomic radii of period 2 (pm)?
Atomic radius across a period and why?
cards.definition: Decreases: same shell, Zeff increases

cards.term: Atomic radius down a group and why?
cards.definition: Increases: n increases and inner shells shield

cards.term: Atomic radii down group 1 and group 17 (pm)?
Why is a cation smaller than its atom?
cards.definition: Fewer electrons, same nuclear charge (Na 186 → Na⁺ 95 pm)

cards.term: Why is an anion larger than its atom?
cards.definition: Extra electron → more repulsion, lower Zeff (F 64 → F⁻ 136 pm)

cards.term: What are isoelectronic species?
cards.definition: Atoms/ions with the same number of electrons, e.g. O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺, Mg²⁺ (10 e⁻)

cards.term: Radius trend among isoelectronic ions?
cards.definition: Greater positive charge → smaller; greater negative charge → larger

cards.term: Increasing ionic radius: N³⁻, O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺, Mg²⁺, Al³⁺? (Ex 3.12)
cards.definition: Al³⁺ < Mg²⁺ < Na⁺ < F⁻ < O²⁻ < N³⁻

cards.term: Largest and smallest: Mg, Mg²⁺, Al, Al³⁺? (Problem 3.5)
cards.definition: Largest Mg; smallest Al³⁺

cards.term: Isoelectronic partners of F⁻, Ar, Mg²⁺, Rb⁺? (Ex 3.11)
cards.definition: F⁻: Na⁺/Ne. Ar: Cl⁻/K⁺. Mg²⁺: Na⁺/Ne. Rb⁺: Br⁻/Kr.

cards.term: Define first ionization enthalpy.
cards.definition: Energy to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻

cards.term: Why "isolated gaseous atom in ground state" in the definition? (Ex 3.14)
cards.definition: So values are comparable: no neighbour interactions, same starting state

cards.term: Why is ΔᵢH₂ > ΔᵢH₁?
cards.definition: Harder to remove an electron from a positive ion than from a neutral atom

cards.term: Is ionization enthalpy ever negative?
cards.definition: No: energy is always required

cards.term: Where are maxima and minima in the ΔᵢH vs Z plot?
cards.definition: Maxima at noble gases; minima at alkali metals

cards.term: ΔᵢH trend across a period and down a group?
cards.definition: Increases across; decreases down

cards.term: Why does ΔᵢH increase across a period?
cards.definition: Nuclear charge rises but shielding barely increases (same shell)

cards.term: Why does ΔᵢH decrease down a group?
cards.definition: Electron farther away; increased shielding outweighs rising nuclear charge

cards.term: Why is ΔᵢH of B < Be?
cards.definition: B loses a 2p electron, more shielded and less penetrating than Be’s 2s

cards.term: Why is ΔᵢH of O < N?
cards.definition: O has a paired 2p electron (extra repulsion); N’s 2p³ is half-filled

cards.term: Actual order of ΔᵢH in period 2?
cards.definition: Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne

cards.term: Al ΔᵢH closer to 575 or 760 kJ/mol? (Problem 3.6: Na 496, Mg 737, Si 786)
cards.definition: 575: Al’s 3p electron is shielded by 3s

cards.term: Na has lower ΔᵢH₁ than Mg but higher ΔᵢH₂. Why? (Ex 3.17)
cards.definition: Na⁺ has a noble gas core (2p⁶); Mg⁺ still has a 3s electron

cards.term: Ionization enthalpy of H in J/mol from E₁ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J? (Ex 3.15)
cards.definition: 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.31 × 10⁶ J mol⁻¹

cards.term: Do two isotopes have the same ΔᵢH? (Ex 3.25)
cards.definition: Yes: same electronic configuration and nuclear charge

cards.term: Why does Ga have higher ΔᵢH than Al? (group 13 anomaly)
cards.definition: Poor shielding by 3d electrons in Ga raises Zeff

cards.term: Define electron gain enthalpy.
cards.definition: Enthalpy change when a neutral gaseous atom gains an electron: X(g) + e⁻ → X⁻(g)

cards.term: Why do halogens have very negative ΔegH?
cards.definition: Gaining one electron gives a noble gas configuration

cards.term: Why do noble gases have positive ΔegH?
cards.definition: The electron must enter the next higher shell

cards.term: ΔegH trend across a period and down a group?
cards.definition: More negative across; less negative down

cards.term: Why is ΔegH of F less negative than Cl (and O than S)?
cards.definition: Added electron enters the small n = 2 shell: strong repulsion

cards.term: Most negative ΔegH of all elements?
cards.definition: Chlorine (−349 kJ/mol)

cards.term: Most and least negative ΔegH: P, S, Cl, F? (Problem 3.7)
cards.definition: Most: Cl; least: P

cards.term: Is the second electron gain enthalpy of O positive? (Ex 3.21)
cards.definition: Positive: adding e⁻ to O⁻ faces strong repulsion

cards.term: Electron affinity vs electron gain enthalpy (footnote)?
cards.definition: Aₑ = −ΔegH (sign reversed); strictly defined at 0 K: ΔegH = −Aₑ − 5/2 RT

cards.term: Define electronegativity.
cards.definition: Ability of an atom in a compound to attract shared electrons; not measurable

cards.term: Electron gain enthalpy vs electronegativity? (Ex 3.22)
cards.definition: ΔegH: isolated atom, measurable. EN: bonded atom, relative, not measurable.

cards.term: Three electronegativity scales?
cards.definition: Pauling (most used), Mulliken-Jaffe, Allred-Rochow

cards.term: Pauling’s reference value?
cards.definition: Fluorine = 4.0 (assigned in 1922)

cards.term: Pauling EN of period 2 and period 3?
Is the EN of N always 3.0? (Ex 3.23)
cards.definition: No: EN varies with the atom it is bonded to (and hybridisation)

cards.term: Link between EN and metallic character?
cards.definition: EN is directly related to non-metallic and inversely to metallic character

cards.term: Figure 3.7 · Periodic trends (name each arrow)
Mnemonic for trends? (intuition)
cards.definition: "Size goes down-left, everything else goes up-right": IE, EN, |ΔegH| rise towards F; radius rises towards Cs

cards.term: Valence of representative elements?
cards.definition: Number of valence electrons, or 8 − valence electrons

cards.term: Oxidation state of O in OF₂ and Na₂O?
cards.definition: +2 in OF₂ (F more EN); −2 in Na₂O

cards.term: Define oxidation state (NCERT).
cards.definition: Charge acquired by an atom on the basis of electronegativity of other atoms in the molecule

cards.term: Formulas from Si + Br and Al + S? (Problem 3.8)
cards.definition: SiBr₄ and Al₂S₃

cards.term: Hydride and oxide formulas across groups (Table 3.9)?
cards.definition: e.g. LiH, CaH₂, B₂H₆, CH₄, NH₃, H₂O, HF; Li₂O, MgO, B₂O₃, CO₂, N₂O₃, SO₃, Cl₂O₇

cards.term: Oxidation state vs covalency of Al in [AlCl(H₂O)₅]²⁺? (Problem 3.9)
cards.definition: Oxidation state +3; covalency 6

cards.term: What is the diagonal relationship?
cards.definition: Similarity of Li with Mg and Be with Al

cards.text: Second-period elements behave anomalously due to {{c1::small size}}, large {{c2::charge/radius ratio}}, high {{c3::electronegativity}} and only {{c4::four}} valence orbitals (2s, 2p).

cards.term: Maximum covalency of B vs Al?
cards.definition: B: 4 ([BF₄]⁻). Al: 6 ([AlF₆]³⁻), using d orbitals.

cards.term: What bonding is special to second-period p-block elements?
cards.definition: pπ–pπ multiple bonds (C=C, C≡C, N≡N, C=O, C≡N)

cards.term: Where in a period is reactivity highest and lowest?
cards.definition: Highest at the two extremes (alkali metals, halogens); lowest in the centre

cards.term: Oxide nature across a period?
cards.definition: Basic (left, e.g. Na₂O) → amphoteric/neutral (centre) → acidic (right, e.g. Cl₂O₇)

cards.term: Examples of amphoteric and neutral oxides?
cards.definition: Amphoteric: Al₂O₃, As₂O₃. Neutral: CO, NO, N₂O.

cards.term: Show Na₂O is basic and Cl₂O₇ acidic. (Problem 3.10)
cards.definition: Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH; Cl₂O₇ + H₂O → 2HClO₄

cards.term: Reactivity order in group 1 vs group 17? (Ex 3.28)
cards.definition: Group 1: Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs (easier e⁻ loss). Group 17: F > Cl > Br > I (easier e⁻ gain).

cards.term: Change in atomic radius across 3d and 4f series?
cards.definition: Much smaller than for representative elements; smallest for 4f

cards.term: Trend in transition metals down a group?
cards.definition: Reverse of main groups: metallic character does not rise (explained by size and IE)

cards.term: Periodic trends summary
cards.definition: Atomic radius: → decreases; ↓ increases; Ionization enthalpy: → increases; ↓ decreases; Electron gain enthalpy: → more negative; ↓ less negative; Electronegativity: → increases; ↓ decreases; Metallic character: → decreases; ↓ increases

cards.term: History of periodic classification
cards.definition: Triads (1829): Dobereiner; Cylindrical table (1862): de Chancourtois; Octaves (1865): Newlands; Periodic law by atomic weight (1869): Mendeleev (and Lothar Meyer); Atomic number as basis (1913): Moseley
